extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of GAP doing computations with finitely presented semigroups/monoids and transformations (mathematicians, computational algebraists, package authors).
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for creating, inspecting, and manipulating finitely presented semigroups/monoids and finite transformations in GAP, including rewriting systems (Knuth–Bendix), equality/word-problem considerations, and concrete transformation operations/attributes. Covers function semantics, expected return values, failure conditions, default behaviors, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup / IsSubmonoidFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if t is a finitely presented semigroup or a subsemigroup of a finitely presented semigroup (similarly for monoids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally such a subsemigroup/monoid can be constructed with Semigroup(gens) or Monoid(gens) where gens is a list of elements of a finitely presented semigroup/monoid. A submonoid of a monoid has the same identity as the monoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFpSemigroup / IsFpMonoid (synonym semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFpSemigroup(s) is a synonym for IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup(s) and IsWholeFamily(s); similarly for monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: a subsemigroup of a finitely presented semigroup is not necessarily finitely presented, so both conditions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsElementOfFpSemigroup / IsElementOfFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if elm is an element of a finitely presented semigroup or monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test membership of elements in finitely presented structures; examples show false/true cases after quotienting the free object by relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the finitely presented group, monoid or semigroup to which an element elm belongs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to recover the ambient finitely presented object from an element; examples show equality checks like m = FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement(m.1 * m.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating fp semigroups/monoids via \/ / operator
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation \/(F, rels) (or F / rels) creates a finitely presented semigroup or monoid given by the presentation ⟨gens | rels⟩, with rels entered as pairs of words in the free generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rels is a list of pairs of words; example constructs fs / [ [ x1*x2*x1, x1 ], [ x2^4, x1 ] ].

rubrics_metrics.name: FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations / FactorFreeMonoidByRelations
rubrics_metrics.description: For a free semigroup/monoid f and a list rels of pairs of elements, returns the quotient by the least congruence generated by rels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware these functions are not called by \/ and may be removed; documentation warns the code needs substantial revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismFpSemigroup / IsomorphismFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finitely presented monoid m or group g, returns an isomorphism from m or g to a finitely presented semigroup or monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned object is a MappingByFunction with forward and backward functions; examples illustrate mapping from group/monoid to corresponding fp object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality test \= for elements of a f.p. semigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Two elements a, b of a finitely presented semigroup are equal if equal in the semigroup; however they may be represented by different words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to fundamental undecidability/complexity issues, the equality test may take a very long time and cannot be guaranteed to finish (see comments on the word problem in section 52.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingElement
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingElement(elm) returns the word from the free semigroup or free monoid used as a representative for elm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain the representative word; Example shows IsWord false on element but true after UnderlyingElement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementOfFpSemigroup / ElementOfFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a family fam of elements of an fp semigroup/monoid and a word in the free generators, returns the element of the fp object with that representative word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations are inverse to UnderlyingElement. Example demonstrates membership tests in free monoid vs quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeSemigroupOfFpSemigroup / FreeMonoidOfFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the underlying free semigroup or free monoid over which the finitely presented semigroup/monoid is defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the free semigroup/monoid generated by the free generators provided by FreeGeneratorsOfFpSemigroup/FreeGeneratorsOfFpMonoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeGeneratorsOfFpSemigroup / FreeGeneratorsOfFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the underlying free generators corresponding to the generators of the finitely presented semigroup or monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps to obtain the generators used in the presentation; used together with RelationsOfFpSemigroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: RelationsOfFpSemigroup / RelationsOfFpMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the relations of the finitely presented semigroup/monoid as pairs of words in the free generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows RelationsOfFpSemigroup(s) returning list of word pairs; useful for inspecting the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confluent rewriting system implies solvable word problem
rubrics_metrics.description: If an fp semigroup/monoid has a confluent rewriting system then it has a solvable word problem: there is an algorithm to decide when two words represent the same element by reducing both words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP uses confluent rewriting systems (when available) to check equality in finitely presented semigroups/monoids by reducing words to normal forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReducedConfluentRewritingSystem (termination and defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: ReducedConfluentRewritingSystem(S[, ordering]) returns a reduced confluent rewriting system for S with respect to a reduction ordering; default ordering is shortlex (length+lexicographic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may not terminate; if S does not have a solvable word problem the procedure will never end. If it does not terminate, returned object is immutable. The attribute also stores the rewriting system. Example and note: different orderings may affect termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knuth–Bendix procedure implementation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP's creation of a reduced confluent rewriting system uses the Knuth–Bendix procedure for strings, which attempts to make a rewriting system confluent; termination is not guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reduction ordering must be specified (shortlex default). The procedure may terminate for one ordering and not another. On Unix, alternative KB implementations (e.g., kbmag) can be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: KB_REW global variable
rubrics_metrics.description: KB_REW is a global record variable whose components contain functions used for Knuth–Bendix; default KB_REW is GAPKB_REW provided by the GAP library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can replace KB_REW to customize KB functions (e.g., to use external KB implementations).

rubrics_metrics.name: KnuthBendixRewritingSystem operation
rubrics_metrics.description: KnuthBendixRewritingSystem(s, wordord) returns the Knuth–Bendix rewriting system of the finitely presented semigroup s (or monoid m) using the reduction ordering wordord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a reduction ordering; behavior similar to ReducedConfluentRewritingSystem but as an operation to invoke the KB routine explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: SemigroupOfRewritingSystem / MonoidOfRewritingSystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the semigroup or monoid over which a rewriting system rws is defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to retrieve the ambient fp object from a rewriting system; examples show equality checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeSemigroupOfRewritingSystem / FreeMonoidOfRewritingSystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the free semigroup or free monoid over which a rewriting system rws is defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps relate rules in rws back to words in the underlying free structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use confluent rewriting system to decide equality (practical guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a confluent rewriting system is available, reduce both representative words using the rules and compare reduced forms to decide equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates ReducedForm(rws, UnderlyingElement(x)) giving identical reduced words for equal elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Todd–Coxeter procedure (transformation representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Todd-Coxeter procedure provides a standard way to find a transformation representation of a finitely presented semigroup; usually one uses IsomorphismTransformationSemigroup instead of calling it directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document notes the procedure exists and where to find higher-level wrappers in GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableOfFpSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right congruence r of an fp-semigroup S, CosetTableOfFpSemigroup(r) is the coset table representing S as transformations on congruence classes; table[i][s] contains image of coset s under generator i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes internal representation of transformation action on cosets; useful for Todd-Coxeter and transformation representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation concept and degree (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A transformation in GAP is a function from positive integers to positive integers acting on the right; the degree of f is the largest n such that n^f != n or i^f = n for some i != n (least n fixing [n+1,n+2,...] pointwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior changed since GAP 4.7 to fix unspecified points, allowing multiplication of arbitrary transformations; degree can be accessed via DegreeOfTransformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation storage representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Internally a transformation f is stored as a list of images i^f up to a value at least the degree; if degree <= 65536 images stored as 16-bit integers (IsTrans2Rep) else 32-bit integers (IsTrans4Rep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kernel and image set are plain lists of GAP integers; representation choice affects memory and category membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsTransformation category and basic ops
rubrics_metrics.description: Every transformation belongs to category IsTransformation; basic operations include ImageListOfTransformation, ImageSetOfTransformation, FlatKernelOfTransformation, RankOfTransformation, DegreeOfTransformation, multiplication, exponentiation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standard functions to query and manipulate transformations; see referenced sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation(list) / TransformationList argument requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Transformation(list) or TransformationList(list) returns transformation f with i^f = list[i] for i in 1..Length(list) and fixes larger points; list must be dense, contain positive integers, and values must be in [1..Length(list)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An error occurs if list is not dense or contains invalid entries. Transformation(list, func) variant uses func to map elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation(src, dst) / TransformationListList
rubrics_metrics.description: If src and dst are lists of positive integers of same length and src has no duplicate elements, TransformationListList(src, dst) returns a transformation f with src[i]^f = dst[i] and fixes points larger than max entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformation is a synonym when args are two lists; analogous to MappingPermListList in permutation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransformationByImageAndKernel preconditions and return
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns f where i^f = im[ker[i]] for i in 1..Length(ker); im must be duplicate-free and ker must be the flat kernel of a transformation with rank equal to Length(im).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If arguments do not fulfil these conditions, fail is returned. Example shows typical usage and returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idempotent(im, ker) behavior and existence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Idempotent(im, ker) returns the idempotent transformation with image set im and flat kernel ker if such exists, otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More specifically im must have one element in every kernel class corresponding to ker and ker must be a valid flat kernel of a transformation with rank equal to length of im. Note: it may return a different transformation than TransformationByImageAndKernel with same args.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransformationOp / TransformationOpNC
rubrics_metrics.description: TransformationOp(obj, list[, func]) returns the transformation corresponding to action of obj on domain list via func (default OnPoints); TransformationOpNC does no checks and should be used cautiously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If obj does not map elements of list into list, fail is returned. Use NC version only when correctness of arguments is guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: TransformationNumber / NumberTransformation bijection
rubrics_metrics.description: Implements a bijection between transformations with degree at most n and numbers in [1..n^n]; TransformationNumber(m,n) returns m-th transformation, NumberTransformation(f,n) returns numeric index of f (n default degree of f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful: numeric values can be very large; example demonstrates mapping back and forth with different n values.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomTransformation(n) returns a random transformation with degree at most n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for sampling; example shows a random transformation of degree 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: IdentityTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: IdentityTransformation is bound to the identity transformation, which has degree 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global variable; use as the identity element for composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConstantTransformation(m, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a constant transformation f such that i^f = n for all i ≤ m when m and n are positive integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates constant transformations for given bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsTransformation conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: AsTransformation(f[, n]) converts permutations, transformations, partial permutations, or binary relations to a transformation with specified semantics depending on type and optional n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permutations: restrict to [1..n] or largest moved point if n omitted. Transformations: restrict to [1..n] if n < degree. PartialPerms: maps undefined points to n and extends to degree m determined by moved points/images. Binary relations: if they define a transformation, return that transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedTransformation(f, list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the transformation g with i^g = i^f for i in list, and i^g = i for i not in list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to restrict action of f to a specified subset; example shows behavior on selected indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermutationOfImage
rubrics_metrics.description: If transformation f permutes the points in its image, PermutationOfImage(f) returns that permutation, otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f is already a permutation, this matches AsPermutation(f). Examples show both fail and success cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator i^f (image), f^g (conjugation by permutation)
rubrics_metrics.description: i ^ f returns the image of positive integer i under f. For f transformation and g permutation, f ^ g returns g^-1 * f * g (conjugation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjugation implemented efficiently; documented as costing similar to multiplying a transformation by a permutation rather than computing inverse first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication and quotient operators for transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: f * g returns composition when f and g are transformations or permutations. f / g returns f * g^-1 when g is a permutation. LeftQuotient(g,f) returns g^-1 * f when g is a permutation and f a transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product of permutation and transformation is returned as a transformation. Document notes relative operation costs (optimized compared to computing inverses explicitly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexicographic and equality comparisons for transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: f < g returns true if image list of f is lexicographically less than image list of g. f = g returns true if transformations equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for ordering and equality checks; relies on image lists (ImageListOfTransformation).

rubrics_metrics.name: PermLeftQuoTransformation / PermLeftQuoTransformationNC
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the permutation on the image set of f induced by f^-1 * g when f and g have equal kernel and image set. The NC variant does not perform checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PermLeftQuoTransformation verifies equal kernels and image sets and errors if not; NC version skips checks and can be used when invariants are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInjectiveListTrans(list, obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true iff obj (a transformation or an image list) is injective on the given list of positive integers; returns false if list has duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If obj supplied is an image list, it is converted via Transformation(obj). Example shows true/false behaviors and duplicate-list detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComponentTransformationInt(f, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the elements of the component of f containing n that can be obtained by applying powers of f to n, i.e., those i such that n^f^j = i for some j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compute connected component in the functional digraph representation; examples show multiple cases including isolated points.

rubrics_metrics.name: PreImagesOfTransformation(f, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the preimages of n under f, i.e., all positive integers i such that i^f = n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows multiple preimages and behavior when n not moved (returns [n] for fixed points beyond degree).

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeOfTransformation / DegreeOfTransformationCollection
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeOfTransformation(f) returns the degree as defined (largest n with n^f != n or i^f = n for some i != n). For a collection, returns maximum degree among transformations in the collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show degree 0 for IdentityTransformation and computing degree across a list of transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageListOfTransformation / ListTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the list of images [1^f .. n^f] of a transformation f for a given n; if n omitted, uses degree of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogue of ListPerm for permutations; examples demonstrate optional n larger than degree filling in fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageSetOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the sorted set of images of f on [1..n] (duplicates removed); if n omitted uses degree of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate returned set and behavior when n > degree yielding additional fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: RankOfTransformation (for n or a list)
rubrics_metrics.description: When called with positive integer n, returns size of the set of images of f in [1..n]; when called with a list of points, returns size of images on that list. If n omitted, uses degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank measures image size; examples show rank over full domain, over larger n, and on specific lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: MovedPoints attribute (transformation and collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: MovedPoints(f) returns the points moved by transformation f; MovedPoints(coll) returns moved points for a collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an attribute in the index of transformation attributes (full description continues beyond this chunk). Use to find points at which f does not act as identity.
